title: The equivalence of topological indices for $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric quantum spin chains
abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases in quantum spin chains are distinguished by topological indices. Ogata's operator-algebraic indices apply to a broad range of symmetry classes without requiring continuous symmetry, whereas the elementary twist index of Tasaki requires $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry. We prove their equivalence in the common setting of integer-spin chains with on-site $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry and a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, without assuming translation invariance or a matrix product representation. A charge-fluctuation estimate yields a strong-limit construction of half-chain rotations with their phases fixed. An exact group commutator identity then identifies the Ogata index with the limit of local twist expectations and gives an explicit error bound. This provides a computable formula when a lower bound on the gap and the relevant ground-state expectations are available. As an application, a previous twist-index calculation determines the Ogata index to be $(-1)^S$ for the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain under explicit uniqueness and boundary-field gap assumptions.   The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy, while ChatGPT made substantial contributions to the development of the proof.
summary: This paper proves the equivalence of two topological indices, the Ogata index and the twist index, for quantum spin chains with $\mathrm{U}(1)times\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. Using advanced techniques from operator algebras and strong convergence estimates, the authors derive a computable formula for this index. This is significant because it provides a robust mathematical framework for characterizing topological order in strongly correlated quantum materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously prove the mathematical equivalence between two distinct topological indices—Ogata's operator-algebraic index ($	ext{IndO}$) and the elementary twist index ($	ext{IndT}$)—for quantum spin chains.
main_result: The equivalence $	ext{IndO} = 	ext{IndT}$ is proven for $\mathrm{U}(1)times\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric integer-spin chains, providing a computable formula for the topological invariant.
method: The proof combines techniques from operator algebras, utilizing a charge-fluctuation estimate to establish strong convergence of half-chain rotations, which is then linked to the Ogata index via an exact group commutator identity.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum spin chains defined on the infinite lattice ($\mathbb{Z}$) with Hamiltonians possessing $\mathrm{U}(1)times\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. The analysis is performed in the ground state ($\omega$) of such a system, assuming it is gapped and locally unique.
key_observables: Topological indices ($	ext{IndO}$, $	ext{IndT}$), local twist expectations ($\omega(T_N)$), and the gap lower bound ($\gamma$).
important_parameters: The symmetry group $\mathrm{U}(1)times\mathbb{Z}_2$, the integer spin value $S$, and the gap $\gamma > 0$.
main_assumptions: The existence of a locally-unique gapped ground state ($\omega$) and the specific $\mathrm{U}(1)times\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry structure are crucial assumptions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the context by defining both indices, then develops the proof by first using charge-fluctuation estimates to prove the strong convergence of half-chain rotations. Finally, an exact group commutator identity is used to equate the two definitions, leading to a computable formula and an application to the Heisenberg chain.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, mathematically rigorous tool to characterize topological order in 1D quantum magnets, extending index theory beyond simple symmetry constraints and offering concrete, computable methods for determining topological invariants.
